question: What is the primary purpose of applying management functions in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Eliminating the need for direct clinical supervision
options.B: Reducing hospital operational costs below government budgets
options.C: Coordinating resources to achieve quality patient care
options.D: Solely focusing on physician administrative demands

explanation: Management functions exist fundamentally to organize human and material assets so that patients receive safe, effective, and timely care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why are management functions viewed as a continuous cycle rather than isolated tasks?

options.A: Because nursing shifts must rotate every eight hours without exception
options.B: Because evaluating outcomes in controlling feeds directly back into future planning
options.C: Because hospital management software automatically deletes completed tasks
options.D: Because government policies prohibit changing administrative duties mid-year

explanation: The management process is dynamic; data gathered during evaluation and control stages inform the next cycle of planning and organizing. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h1)

question: What distinguishes operational plans from strategic plans in a hospital environment?

options.A: Operational plans dictate daily ward routines, while strategic plans look years ahead
options.B: Operational plans are temporary drafts, while strategic plans are permanent laws
options.C: Operational plans deal with finances, while strategic plans deal only with sanitation
options.D: Operational plans are handled exclusively by doctors, while strategic plans are for nurses

explanation: Operational planning focuses on immediate, short-term daily activities, whereas strategic planning sets long-term institutional goals. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h2)

question: A ward manager anticipates a seasonal surge in malaria admissions for the upcoming rainy season. Which management function is this nurse actively demonstrating?
explanation: Anticipating future healthcare needs and preparing proactive measures before a crisis occurs is the core essence of planning. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of the organizing function in nursing management?

options.A: Disciplining staff members who arrive late to duty
options.B: Structuring authority and workflow to execute plans
options.C: Writing long-term financial budgets for the hospital board
options.D: Diagnosing complex medical pathologies in patients

explanation: Organizing establishes the structural framework, reporting lines, and workflow patterns needed to turn established plans into action. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h3)

question: How does proper ergonomic arrangement of ward supplies directly support nursing management?

options.A: It eliminates the requirement for routine equipment maintenance checks
options.B: It reduces unnecessary movement and cuts down response times during emergencies
options.C: It prevents patients from leaving the hospital ward without permission
options.D: It guarantees an automatic increase in monthly hazard allowances

explanation: Organizing physical space efficiently removes operational friction, allowing nurses to access tools quickly when seconds matter. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which patient care model divides duties by specific tasks, such as assigning one nurse exclusively to administer all ward medications?
explanation: Functional nursing breaks care down into discrete tasks assigned to different individuals, which is often utilized during severe staff shortages. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the defining characteristic of primary nursing as a care delivery model?

options.A: All healthcare decisions are made exclusively by senior resident medical doctors
options.B: Unskilled nursing assistants independently manage complex surgical wards overnight
options.C: Staff members rotate tasks randomly every hour to prevent occupational boredom
options.D: One registered nurse maintains 24-hour accountability for a patient's care plan from admission to discharge

explanation: Primary nursing centres on individual accountability, where a designated nurse coordinates comprehensive care even when off duty through detailed planning. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which managerial function primarily addresses interpersonal guidance, communication, and staff motivation?
explanation: Directing deals directly with human interactions, leadership styles, communication channels, and motivating personnel to perform their duties well. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why are intrinsic motivators such as recognition and supportive supervision important in nursing management?

options.A: They completely replace the legal requirement to pay monthly salaries on time
options.B: They allow nurse managers to bypass hospital safety audits and licensing exams
options.C: They ensure that patients recover from surgical procedures in half the normal time
options.D: They help sustain staff morale and retention when working conditions are stressful

explanation: Intrinsic rewards build psychological resilience, helping healthcare workers remain committed despite systemic challenges and heavy workloads. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of the controlling function in healthcare administration?

options.A: Designing brand new architectural layouts for emergency wards
options.B: Setting the strategic five-year financial budget for hospital expansion
options.C: Monitoring performance against standards and implementing corrective actions
options.D: Punishing healthcare workers immediately after any minor workplace mistake

explanation: Controlling ensures that actual clinical practice aligns with established benchmarks, correcting deviations to maintain high standards of care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h6)

question: How should a nurse manager ideally respond to an incident report involving a near-miss medication error?

options.A: Investigate underlying system vulnerabilities rather than defaulting to punitive blame
options.B: Hide the incident report from hospital directors to protect the ward's reputation
options.C: Ignore the event if no actual patient harm occurred during the administration
options.D: Suspend all nursing students working on the shift without an official hearing

explanation: Modern quality improvement frameworks emphasize a just culture that examines systemic flaws rather than discouraging reporting through fear of punishment. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary function of communication tools like SBAR in multi-disciplinary healthcare teams?

options.A: Eliminating the need for shift handover reports at the nursing station
options.B: Replacing all written patient case notes with verbal telephone calls
options.C: Facilitating structured, objective, and prompt collaborative problem-solving
options.D: Permitting nurses to independently prescribe specialized surgical medications

explanation: SBAR provides a standardized framework that streamlines communication among different healthcare professionals during critical patient updates. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why is coordination considered a vital responsibility for nurse managers within multi-disciplinary teams?

options.A: It prevents other healthcare departments from having any meetings on hospital premises
options.B: It ensures that nurses have complete legal authority over physician treatment orders
options.C: It synchronizes diverse professional efforts to prevent gaps and duplication in patient care
options.D: It guarantees that all patients are discharged within forty-eight hours of admission

explanation: Because multiple specialists care for the same patient, coordination bridges professional silos to deliver cohesive, safe, and holistic treatment. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h7)
